findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so captured logs are dropped
findings.body: `FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, not `f`. Code that logs through `logger.FromContext(ctx)` (as `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now does at `logger_middleware.go:58`) writes to a throwaway instance. Assertions on `InfoLogs`/`ErrorLogs` of the logger passed in would then see nothing. No current test hits this. Returning `f` would keep captured calls observable and match what the real `FromContext` does when no contextual attributes are present.

findings.title: No tests for the new middleware or for the traceID/attribute move
findings.body: The PR moves context enrichment out of the metrics middleware and drops the explicit `traceID` param from the request log. The log line now relies on the `FromContext` providers registered in `pkg/infra/log/log.go:55` and `pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:91`. No test covers the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`. No test checks that `Plugin Request Completed` still carries pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname and traceID. A small test that passes a context through the middleware and asserts `log.WithContextualAttributes` data is present would guard this refactor.

findings.title: Test name still says Instrumentation
findings.body: The type and constructor were renamed to `MetricsMiddleware`/`newMetricsMiddleware`, but the test function is still `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`. Renaming it to `TestMetricsMiddleware` would keep the naming consistent.

contracts.action: Plugin request context enrichment moved from the metrics middleware into a new ContextualLoggerMiddleware, placed after metrics and before the logger middleware
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously `InstrumentationMiddleware.instrumentPluginRequest` called `instrumentContext` (after the plugin-target lookup) and then `fn(ctx)`. The same attribute set (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) is now built in `contextual_logger_middleware.go:27-37` for QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics.
contracts.before_after: Before: attributes were added only when `pluginTarget` succeeded, otherwise the call returned ErrPluginNotRegistered early. After: attributes are always added, and the metrics middleware still returns early on an unregistered plugin before reaching it. The logger middleware sits after the new middleware, so its context carries the attributes. Stream endpoints were not instrumented before and still are not. The removed doc comment on the metrics middleware said it must be at the top of the stack; the order tracing, metrics, contextual logger, logger keeps the contextual logger ahead of every consumer that logs.
contracts.visible_effect: `Plugin Request Completed` log lines keep pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname and, via the tracing provider, traceID. The code now emits them through `FromContext` instead of explicit params.
contracts.failure_mode: If the tracing service is not provided (providers are registered in `tracing.ProvideService`), traceID is silently absent from the log line. Before, `tracing.TraceIDFromContext` was called directly. In normal Grafana startup the provider is registered.

contracts.action: New plog.Logger.FromContext on grafanaInfraLogWrapper, delegating to ConcreteLogger.FromContext
contracts.equivalent_path: `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` in pkg/infra/log/log.go:203 runs all registered ctx providers and returns `cl.New(args...)`, or `cl` itself when there are none.
contracts.before_after: The wrapper type-asserts the result to `*log.ConcreteLogger`. Both branches of `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` return `*ConcreteLogger`, so the assertion succeeds and the wrapper keeps the same underlying logger plus the context args. The `!ok` fallback `d.New()` is unreachable with this implementation and would drop the context if hit.
contracts.visible_effect: Request log lines include context attributes. No other implementer of `plog.Logger` exists besides the wrapper and `TestLogger`, so the interface change compiles across the repo.
contracts.failure_mode: None found. With no providers matching, the original logger is returned and the log is unchanged.

summary: The refactor looks behavior-preserving. The context attributes now come from a separate ContextualLoggerMiddleware placed after the metrics middleware. `FromContext` is added to the plugin logger interface and wrapper, and the traceID comes from the registered tracing log provider. I found no defects. I left three low-severity notes: the fake `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a new instance and drops logs, the new middleware has no tests, and the test function name still says "Instrumentation".
